::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 5th 1888  
**From:** Elderfield  
**Manuscript:** MS Miss Barbara Dennis/6
:::

My dear [Miss Bourne](people/person_1379.qmd)

Indeed I would gladly if I could, but months ago [Professor Freeman](people/person_523.qmd)asked me to come and see Hannah Mores villages, and hear his recollections of her, and the time has fixed itself for next week, and after that comes harvest - and dedication feasts - and Mission Guild meeting, and I am afraid I cannot do it  though I am very sorry not to see you again this year before you are shut up for the winter. If you were well enough I might manage a day or two later.  My [National Society](organizations/other_32.qmd)story I fancy you will like being the history of a young school mistress and pupil teachers.[^1]  We have just had a grand wedding here of [our master](people/person_1256.qmd)and [Alice Misselbrook](people/person_1257.qmd)after being infant mistress nine years.[^2]  She gives up which is better for him than for us and we are expecting her successor.

Of worthy books, you should read [the Dragon of the North](other_books/otherbook_1062.qmd).  It is like a possible Fouqué

your affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Silurian envelope addressed to 'Miss Sturges Bourne/ Crookham Knole/ Farnham' and postmarked Winchester 5 September 1888 and Farnham 6 September 1888.
[^2]: This was CMY's *Our New Mistress, or, Changes at Brookfield Earl* (London, National Society 1888).
[^3]: Alice Misselbrook, the mistress of Otterbourne Girls' School, married Alfred Rolfe, who taught the boys.
